verdict.rationale: mise documents a registry of 1,000+ tools with shorthands, searchable via `mise search` [mise-docs-113, mise-docs-16, mise-docs-31, mise-docs-93]. It also has many backends, including npm, pipx/PyPI, cargo, GitHub releases, aqua, its own Homebrew implementation and generic http, which together give access to 'almost all programs available on GitHub' [mise-docs-104, mise-docs-54, mise-docs-57, mise-docs-38, mise-docs-94, mise-docs-26]. Users independently confirm the broad package sources and frequent releases, and floating registry data lets users get current tool definitions without upgrading mise [mise-comm-19, mise-comm-6, mise-comm-11, mise-docs-72]. Missing for 10: no explicit evidence of how the registry itself is curated or how often it is updated, beyond release frequency.
